source_review.notes: Checked eight official or primary sources. RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 define and disambiguate uppercase normative keywords. RFC 9110 defines HTTP semantics that local style cannot contradict. RFC 9457 defines problem details and the application/problem+json media type without authorizing sensitive detail disclosure. The OpenAPI Specification defines a machine-readable HTTP API description but does not prescribe a local resource or governance profile. Google publishes general and service-specific AIPs. Microsoft's former general guideline redirects teams to scoped Azure and Graph guidance; the current Azure document explicitly scopes itself to Azure data-plane APIs. Zalando publishes REST and event guidance with rule IDs and normative levels. External guide rules are treated as examples/evidence, not universal requirements.

evidence: Checked guide version G_v, applicable rules R(a), mandatory subset M(a), advisory subset A(a), pass predicate p(a,r), and exception predicate x(a,r).
Confirmed mandatory conformance is a conjunction over applicable rules plus evidence freshness.
Confirmed weighted advisory score requires a positive denominator and is explicitly separated from mandatory conformance.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Applicability is evaluated before conformance; exceptions must cover the exact rule and surface and remain valid.

evidence: Recomputed 96 advisory passes plus three mandatory passes as 99 passes among 100 checks, yielding 99%.
Confirmed one of four mandatory rules fails, so only three mandatory rules pass and the mandatory conjunction is false.
Checked example counts of 120 APIs and 3,400 findings as internally consistent scenario inputs.
Confirmed all ten worked examples and five exercise/answer pairs are distinct.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Guide sizes, pass rates, warning counts, API counts, and finding counts are illustrative and not asserted organizational measurements.

evidence: Verified A(a)=R(a) minus M(a) partitions applicable advisory rules when M(a) is a subset of R(a).
Verified C(a) fails when any applicable mandatory rule has neither adequate pass evidence nor a valid exception.
Constructed a 99-pass counterexample where the sole failed rule is object authorization, disproving average-score sufficiency.
Verified two runtime implementations can share one description artifact while differing in GET side effects, disproving artifact-only semantic proof.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The model represents governance logic, not a claim that all API quality dimensions reduce to formal predicates.

evidence: Reviewed public, partner, internal, experimental, legacy, REST/JSON, gRPC, GraphQL, webhook, event, streaming, and long-running surfaces.
Reviewed standards-versus-style conflict, vague normative terms, contradictory/imported rules, unstable IDs, examples that accidentally broaden rules, and non-waivable controls.
Reviewed parser/spec upgrades, false positives/negatives, duplicate diagnostics, baselines, changed-surface gates, suppressions, appeals, exception expiry, and guide/tool/example drift.
Reviewed legacy naming/timestamp compatibility, generator effects, security disclosure, runtime mismatch, emergency changes, metric gaming, missing artifacts, and consumer outcomes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans authority, protocol, scope, behavior, automation, security, compatibility, lifecycle, governance, and measurement.

evidence: Confirmed protocol, security, and legal authorities outrank local style preference.
Confirmed every rule has durable identity, explicit scope/strength, rationale, examples, verification/remediation, ownership, lifecycle, and exception policy.
Confirmed automated claims remain bounded to declared artifacts/tool versions while semantic/runtime evidence receives separate review.
Confirmed guide changes and legacy adoption remain constrained by compatibility, consumer evidence, deprecation, version alignment, and auditable exceptions.
invariant_checking.notes: Consistency is treated as a means to consumer and operational outcomes, not as an authority to erase justified semantic differences.

evidence: Reviewed the precedence argument and confirmed private rules cannot create interoperable redefinitions of standard protocol semantics.
Reviewed the conformance counterexample and confirmed averaging can conceal one fatal mandatory violation.
Reviewed the automation-boundary argument and confirmed artifact equality does not entail runtime behavioral equality.
Reviewed the migration invariant and confirmed new style preferences do not override shipped consumer contracts.
proof_review.notes: The arguments establish bounded governance constraints; they do not claim that a guide mechanically guarantees a good API.

evidence: Confirmed the four formal passages are labeled precedence argument, conformance counterexample, automation boundary argument, and migration invariant.
Confirmed BCP 14 keywords, HTTP, problem details, OpenAPI, and external-guide claims are attributed to their exact scopes.
Confirmed rule IDs, severity, rollout stages, corpus sizes, counts, percentages, and review cycles are local models or scenarios rather than standards mandates.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Protocol fact, external organizational practice, local policy design, analytical reasoning, and empirical outcome evidence remain separate.

evidence: All eight official or primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
The chapter requires actual corpus runs, fixtures, semantic/runtime/security evidence, compatibility impact, consumer research, exception data, appeals, incidents, and adoption outcomes.
No organization's API quality, conformance percentage, linter validity, exception debt, review speed, consumer onboarding, incident rate, or migration readiness is asserted.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Worked examples illustrate governance decisions but cannot substitute for evidence from the scoped API portfolio.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed purpose/scope, authority/precedence, normative language, durable rule records, coherent surface coverage, external profiles, specification-policy separation, automation boundaries, findings/gates, exceptions/appeals, guide evolution, compatibility-safe adoption, and outcome maintenance as one governance system.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through stable rule metadata, applicability predicates, protocol profiles, lint fixtures, deterministic diagnostics, representative corpus testing, baselines, exception records, proposal/change workflows, versioned tools/templates, changed-surface gates, migration recipes, ownership, and operational/consumer metrics.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module progresses from scope and authority through rule construction, API-system coverage, automation and exceptions, then evolution, adoption, and outcomes. Counterexamples prevent score/linter/style overclaims. Ten worked examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, standards-body, legal, security, or practitioner review is claimed.
